IBM.rationale: IBM's Q2 2026 earnings miss is a severe negative event that has fundamentally damaged the investment thesis. Revenue of $17.16B missed consensus by ~$700M (+1% YoY vs. 5%+ guidance), with Z mainframe sales plunging 42% YoY and transaction processing declining 9%. The miss erased ~$68B in market cap and triggered securities investigations into management's disclosure practices. CEO Krishna's admission that customers are 'capex reprioritizing' toward AI infrastructure (servers, memory) away from IBM's software/mainframe stack suggests a structural headwind, not a cyclical timing issue. The abruptness of the guidance cut—from '5-plus percent' to 1% in one quarter—has severely damaged management credibility. While the software franchise retains quality (ARR $24.6B growing 8%, Red Hat +11% sequentially), this is overwhelmed by: (1) the magnitude of the revenue miss and guidance reset, (2) the structural threat of enterprise AI budgets bypassing IBM's stack, (3) elevated leverage (~$62B debt including $13B financing-related) in a 6.32% Baa-yield environment, and (4) deteriorating sentiment with recent news scores of -1.0. The stock's 25%+ drawdown to a 52-week low ($199.19) and P/E compression from ~41x to ~20x reflects genuine fundamental deterioration, not a buying opportunity. The margin expansion from 9.1% to 15.5% net margin is suspect given flat revenue and earnings, likely reflecting non-recurring items rather than sustainable improvement. With earnings yield of 5.1% barely exceeding the 4.68% risk-free rate, there is no valuation cushion. This is a deteriorating business with damaged credibility facing structural headwinds, warranting the most negative rating.
